subject: FluxPay latency & error spike — exec standby / stakeholder update
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@fluxpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@fluxpay.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:04 -0700
Subject: FluxPay: sudden errors + latency spike, need immediate help

Jonas,

We're seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency for LLM inference calls to the model you serve for us. Latency jumped from median ~120ms to ~1.6s and error rate climbed to ~4.2% starting ~08:45 PDT. This is impacting payment authorization flows — we're throttling traffic but still seeing failures.

Attached: telemetry-snapshot-09-12.png (heatmap, error types)

Can you confirm who we should route to at Redwood for an exec-level update? This is elevated to our CTO and CEO.

— Marta
Head of SRE, FluxPay

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@fluxpay.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:25:47 -07:00
Subject: RE: FluxPay: sudden errors + latency spike, need immediate help

Team — FluxPay reporting production-impacting throughput/latency spike with rising 5xxs. Their execs are watching. I am standing up an exec standby and we need triage + a customer-facing cadence. Immediate asks: 1) Laura/David — quick root-cause triage and mitigation plan (10–15 min) 2) Marissa — draft SLA-safe customer note and schedule a 12:00 PDT sync with FluxPay leadership 3) Kimberly — prepare cost/scale options if we need to burst capacity.

I'll coordinate communications. Please reply in-thread with short status updates.

Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@fluxpay.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:40:12 -07:00
Subject: RE: FluxPay: sudden errors + latency spike, need immediate help

Jonas / team — initial findings from telemetry (attached):
- Rapid increase in tail latency correlating with a recent model-routing change (deployed 06:30 PDT) that introduced a fallback policy which forces cross-region model routing when local pool is busy.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~45% on affected calls; concurrent inflight tokens per session spiked.
- Error signature indicates transient OOMs on a subset of GPUs + grpc connection resets.

Immediate mitigation we recommend (now):
1) Roll back routing change (revert to local-only routing) — low blast radius and likely reduces cross-region pressure.
2) Enable per-customer request concurrency cap at the loadbalancer to smooth bursts.
3) Bring up two additional dedicated workers in the us-west pool (manual for now).

I'm attaching telemetry-snapshot-09-12.png for the war-room. I'll start rollback if we get a +1 from infra (David).

— Laura
Senior Infra SRE, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@fluxpay.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:05:30 -07:00
Subject: RE: FluxPay: sudden errors + latency spike, need immediate help

Laura / team — executing mitigation now:
- Rolling back routing change deployed 06:30 PDT (command run at 10:02 PDT). Expected effect: local routing resumes, should reduce cross-region tail latency within a couple minutes.
- Spun up 2x us-west d-inference nodes, added to FluxPay pool; health checks green.
- Enabled temporary concurrency cap (per-customer) of 8 concurrent requests for FluxPay.

Results so far (10:04 PDT): median latency dropping toward 180–240ms; 5xx rate trending down from 4.2% to 1.1%. Still monitoring for full stabilization.

Playbook refs: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INC-8723 (runbook), incident-timeline-fluxpay-20270630.pdf (draft attached).

— David
VP, Serving Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@fluxpay.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:20:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: FluxPay: sudden errors + latency spike, need immediate help

Marta / Jonas — draft customer note for approval (short):

Hi Marta,

Thank you for flagging this — we apologize for the disruption. Our on-call and infra teams identified a routing change that drove increased cross-region traffic and degraded cache efficiency. We have rolled back that change, increased dedicated capacity in us-west, and applied a temporary concurrency cap to protect your production traffic.

Current status (11:15 PDT): error rates reduced materially and median latency is nearing baseline. We are continuing to monitor and will share a detailed incident timeline and corrective actions within 3 business days. We propose a 12:00 PDT executive sync to review impact and next steps.

Attached: mutual-action-plan-fluxpay.xlsx (proposed short-term and medium-term actions).

If this looks good I'll send to FluxPay and confirm the 12:00 slot.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@fluxpay.com>, ceo@fluxpay.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: FluxPay — status update and next steps (post-mitigation)

Marta / FluxPay leadership —

Quick status update following this morning's incident:
- What happened: a routing change increased cross-region calls and reduced KV cache effectiveness, producing higher tail latency and elevated 5xxs for a subset of traffic.
- What we did: rolled back the routing change, provisioned 2 additional us-west workers, and applied a temporary per-customer concurrency cap.
- Current status (12:55 PDT): median latency ~170ms; 5xx down to ~0.6%. We continue to monitor for 3 hours before lifting the concurrency cap.
- Next steps: 1) postmortem and full incident timeline (attached: incident-timeline-fluxpay-20270630.pdf) by EOD 07/02/2027; 2) proposed durable fix in the mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-fluxpay.xlsx) — includes a safer rollout for routing changes, improved canarying for cache regressions, and a short-term capacity reserve for peak windows; 3) 12:00 PDT exec sync (accepted) for any outstanding questions.

We regret the disruption and appreciate the rapid coordination. We'll be transparent about steps to prevent recurrence and will share a bridge link for the 12:00 sync.

Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
